longDescription.intro: This website is an artist portfolio created by my partner in crime and me for our friend and artist, Helene Volle. The portfolio was built to showcase her artwork and projects while giving her a website that reflected her own visual style.
longDescription.motivation:
In 2024, Helene was preparing to apply for a master's program in Italy combining the fields of art and biology. As part of her application, she needed a portfolio where she could present her work. 

 She had started building a portfolio using a drag-and-drop website builder. Although she had created a design she liked, the available tools made it difficult to achieve exactly what she envisioned. During a visit, she asked whether I had experience with web development. My partner and I offered to build the website from scratch instead, and the project started from there.
longDescription.process:
The project had a strict deadline, as Helene needed the portfolio for her master's application. We only had a couple of weeks during our summer break to complete it.

 At the time, I had not yet learned React and was more comfortable working with vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, so we chose to build the website using those technologies. The initial requirements were relatively simple: Helene needed an overview of her projects, an About page, and individual project pages where she could display her artwork in image grids. 

 Since the artwork was the main focus of the portfolio, we prioritized creating a flexible grid system for displaying images. Helene had already developed her own color scheme, wireframes, and logo, and she was closely involved throughout the development process. This allowed us to adapt the website based on her feedback and create something that matched her original vision. 

 As the project developed, we also added: A larger image view when clicking on individual artwork, Navigation between images, Different layouts for smaller and larger projects, Image and file storage using Firebase, A private admin page for managing portfolio content and The admin page is not publicly accessible for security reasons, but screenshots of its functionality can be found below.
futureAdditions: Extended admin functionality: ability to change about-info

longDescription.intro:
This was the Bachelor project for my degree in informatics. The focus is gaining practical experience collaborating within larger developing groups and delivering a software product for real world customers. Our customer was Trondheim kommune, specifically their Human Resources (HR) department, where we were creating a CV scanner. 

 The development team consisted of 7 students, each contributing approximately 15 hours per week. The project spanned from mid-January to early May 2026, giving the team just over three months of active development.
longDescription.motivation: When a department within Trondheim kommune is reorganized or shut down, some of the affected employees are classified as redundant. Being classified as redundant means that after a predefined time period, their position will be removed, and the employee may face termination. According to the Norwegian Work Environment Act (Arbeidsmiljøloven § 15-7), redundant employees must be considered for other available positions within Trondheim kommune before those positions are advertised externally. HR advisors are responsible for managing this internal matching process, manually reviewing employee CVs against job posts to assess suitability.  The goal of this project was to develop a web-based AI tool that assists HR advisors in the internal matching of redundant employees to available positions.
longDescription.process:
We developed a functional prototype capable of evaluating and matching candidates against job postings. A significant part of the project involved investigating which AI model would be most suitable for the CV Screening Tool. The customer specifically requested that NorLLM be considered, as it is developed in Norway and trained on Norwegian-language data. This made it particularly relevant for a system intended to process Norwegian CVs and job postings. To provide a meaningful comparison, we also evaluated Gemini. Gemini offered strong documentation and API support, and members of the team already had experience working with it. Trondheim Kommune also had existing agreements with Google, which could simplify a potential implementation. 

  To evaluate whether the AI produced useful candidate rankings, we collaborated with members of Trondheim Kommune's HR department. HR employees independently ranked a selection of candidates for a job posting, providing us with a human baseline against which we could compare the AI-generated results. The aim was not for the AI to reproduce the rankings exactly, but to determine whether its assessments were reasonably aligned with those of experienced HR personnel. Through extensive testing and comparison of the two models, we found that NorLLM would require further development and training to perform reliably for our specific use case, while Gemini produced more consistent results. 

 Testing was not limited to the AI models. We conducted user testing with potential HR users and iterated on the interface based on their feedback. As Trondheim Kommune is a public-sector organization, accessibility and universal design were important requirements throughout the project. We therefore followed universal design principles and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) referenced by the Norwegian Authority for Universal Design of ICT (UUtilsynet).

 The prototype and our findings were delivered to Trondheim Kommune. Future development and potential implementation of the system will be handled by Trondheim Digital, Trondheim Kommune's IT department.
highlights: Focus on universal design and accessibility testing
Testing: user-testing, unit and end-to-end, AI bias testing and Ground Truth Validation

longDescription.intro: This project was one of two projects developed as part of IT2810 – Web Development at NTNU. The hosted version is currently only accessible through the NTNU network or VPN
longDescription.motivation: Our team developed a recipe application where users can browse recipes, filter by category, sort alphabetically, search for recipes, and use a randomizer for inspiration.
longDescription.process:
The project was developed over approximately two months with four partial deliveries, covering the MVP, data integration, testing, and bug fixing. We used Git issues and Kanban boards to organize and distribute the work. 

 A large part of my work focused on the frontend functionality. I worked on the recipe randomizer, allowing users to discover a random recipe for inspiration, as well as pagination for efficiently browsing larger collections of recipes. I also implemented local and session storage to persist relevant user choices and application state between pages and sessions.

 The application uses MongoDB for data storage, and I was in charge of implementing caching using Redis to reduce unnecessary database requests and improve data retrieval speed.
futureAdditions: Host the page on a public accessible domain
highlights: Testing: end-to-end, component and snapshot tests

longDescription.intro: Henriette Sandven is a specialist in child and adolescent psychiatry, and in 2025 she published the book Diagnosefellen, which discusses how too many children today are being diagnosed and medicated unnecessarily. She has been particularly outspoken in the public ADHD debate, which has received significant attention in Norwegian media. With over 15 years of clinical experience, Henriette has developed a strong professional voice in her field — and, as her name suggests, I am also proud to be her daughter.
longDescription.motivation: Following the publication of Diagnosefellen, Henriette has participated in podcasts, interviews, articles, lectures, and other public appearances. The goal of this project was to gather this content in one place while also providing an easy way for event organizers and media outlets to contact and book her for speaking engagements.
longDescription.process:
I designed and developed diagnosefellen.no from the ground up. The page is complete with the functionalities Henriette required, although the website is still under some development. The site provides a paginated media archive where Henriette's articles, podcasts, interviews, and other appearances can be easily found. I also implemented a booking form and mailing service, allowing speaking and media requests to be sent directly through the website.

 To make the site maintainable without requiring changes to the code, I created a protected admin interface where Henriette can add new media appearances herself. When a link is entered, a script automatically retrieves available metadata such as the title, description, and image and uses it to pre-fill the form. The information can then be reviewed and edited before the post is published.

 The project also includes database integration, authentication, pagination, and functionality for managing media posts.
futureAdditions: Session and local storage for filtering
Henriette is working on a new book, info about this will be added to the page.

longDescription.intro: Social Minds is a startup working to create a more responsible and user-focused social media platform. The platform is designed to encourage intentional use rather than endless scrolling, while prioritizing user privacy and avoiding the sharing or selling of personal data to third parties.
longDescription.motivation:
From the Social Minds website: 'Moderation on social media has long failed to protect us: From violence to misinformation and promotion of eating disorders. On Social Minds, protection is not an “add-on” - it’s our core. Plus, no AI-generated content.' 

 I was drawn to Social Minds because of its focus on building social media around the well-being of its users rather than maximizing engagement. The project also provides an opportunity to explore how software and platform design can encourage healthier online habits while still creating an engaging social experience.
longDescription.process:
Social Minds is  currently a team of six, and I work as a Full-Stack Developer. The internship started during the summer of 2026, and as I found the company's values inspiring and made friends within the team, I decided to stay on the project while pursuing my master's degree. 

 The codebase is private for now, however I encourage to visit the Social Minds website for more info (see link at the top of this page).
futureAdditions: Create algorithms that avoid doom-scrolling on social media platforms and endless content consumption.
Ensure responsible handling of user data, including avoiding the sale or unnecessary sharing of personal data with third parties
Continue exploring design choices that encourage healthier and more intentional use of social media.

longDescription.intro: This is an ongoing hobby project developed together with two classmates from my Informatics degree at NTNU. Unlike our university projects, there are no deadlines or formal requirements, so we work on the application whenever we have time and use it as an opportunity to experiment with new ideas and technologies.
longDescription.motivation:
The idea came from our own experiences with party games. We often found ourselves searching online for question lists, game ideas, or simple tools such as a dice or a deck of cards. We wanted to bring all of these into one application and add the features we felt were missing from existing party game apps. 

 The MVP is now complete and includes collections such as 100 Questions, different party games, a card deck, dice, and a customizable spin-the-wheel game.
longDescription.process:
I have worked on both the functionality and design of the application. A particular focus has been creating reusable components and a theming system that allows the appearance of the entire application to change depending on the selected mode. The application currently supports light and dark mode, but the system is designed to support more distinctive themes in the future. One planned example is a computer science theme using pixel-style icons and programming-inspired fonts. We would also like to create themes inspired by other fields, such as medicine and chemistry, allowing users to personalize the application to their interests.

 Since this is an experimental side project, we are testing vibecoding using AI-assisted development for some smaller and repetitive features. Any generated code is reviewed and adjusted by us before being included in the codebase.

 Our next major feature is a group system, which will allow us to build games around the people participating rather than only providing standalone party-game tools.

 One planned feature is Sidequests, where each person receives individual challenges to complete throughout the evening, such as taking a picture with a stranger. We also want groups to be able to collect and share memorable photos and quotes from the evening within the application.
futureAdditions: Shared photos and quotes within groups
More party games and utilities as we come up with new ideas
